card.change: Ensemble-refine parent attempt 10 with one isolated feature family. Reproduce its attempt-7-equivalent 24-feature member and attempt-8-equivalent 30-feature member, including binary objective, uniform rows, 63 leaves, learning_rate=0.05, 240-round ceiling, final-three-date split, full-data refit, causal user_id/time_ms/physical-order sequence construction, exact within-user GAUC/nDCG@5 round selection on the frozen 20,30,...,240 grid, and within-user average-tie percentile ranks. Add a third 36-feature member that nests the 30 proxy features and appends six categorical fields: dense user code and user crossed separately with current tab, duration bucket, hour, session-position bucket, and preceding proxy state. Build the dense vocabulary from the chronological prefix for holdout training, map unseen users to code 0, rebuild and checkpoint the vocabulary from all training rows for final inference, and log warm-user coverage. Use the frozen 1/8-step three-member simplex, which contains the reconstructed attempt-10 blend at personalized weight 0. Select the best chronological-primary combination with GAUC and proximity-to-parent tie-breaks, but accept nonzero personalization only if its local primary exceeds the reconstructed parent by at least 0.0005; otherwise emit the parent blend. Persist all three boosters, selected rounds and weights, vocabulary, feature contracts, schema/sequence audits, full metric paths, and rank-divergence diagnostics. Final mode loads only the checkpoint and label-free evaluation features.
evidence: STATE:attempt 10 is the current validation best and passed checkpoint replay, with GAUC=0.6750205783133026, nDCG@5=0.6450701950552279, and primary=0.6600453866842653. It is therefore the parent to preserve rather than replace.

STATE:attempt 9 scored GAUC=0.6756235968846531, nDCG@5=0.6438155836477921, and primary=0.6597195902662226. Attempt 10's chronological within-user selection produced a small primary gain with a GAUC/nDCG tradeoff, supporting reuse of its exact metric-aligned selection geometry but arguing for a conservative gate on any extra ensemble degree of freedom.

STATE:attempt 6 removed raw user/content identifiers, metadata, and every target-rate table from attempt 4 and improved primary from 0.5136198093284867 to 0.6194660985246655. This rejects restoration of the bundled sparse mechanisms, but because user-context interactions were removed together with video/author/music/tag features it does not isolate whether dense low-cardinality personalization itself is useful.

The proposed member performs the missing isolation without target-rate tables.

EDA:user-history-density-and-support reports a median 3489 training rows per user, p90 11662, and user long_view rates ranging from 0.0106666667 to 0.832. EDA:tab-context-distribution reports sharply different global rates across dominant tabs: 0.3194828108 on tab 1, 0.0395547152 on tab 0, and 0.4310815981 on tab 4. Personalizing this strong row-varying context is more plausible than adding a user intercept, which cannot change within-user rank.

STATE:attempts 7 and 8 improved the cold-safe context model by adding strictly backward session state and a causal predecessor engagement proxy; attempts 9 and 10 then improved their within-user rank ensemble. The new member nests all 30 established features and adds only interactions around those measured mechanisms.

EDA:validation-cold-item-rate reports 0.7422197404 cold-video rows and EDA:item-frequency-and-tail reports 0.6706248142 singleton training videos. The candidate therefore continues to omit video_id, video metadata, author/music/tag identifiers, and all item target aggregates.

STATE:attempt 4 established uniform pointwise binary learning as stronger than debugged LambdaRank, while attempt 5's per-user class-balanced weighting collapsed primary to 0.4015359629325522. All three members retain uniform binary loss, 63 leaves, deterministic seeds, and chronological primary selection.

STATE:attempt 1 falsified deterministic reconstruction because evaluation_features lacks play_time_ms. The candidate reads only the confirmed inference columns and never uses current or future outcomes.

Source:KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos, recorded in research_plan.json, documents dense per-user sequential behavior. Its applicability is limited here by the absence of the random-exposure log, so this experiment uses only the supplied standard-log user/context fields and makes no propensity claim.
card.falsifier: Reject executability if the dense vocabulary is empty, unsorted, inconsistently encoded, or absent from the checkpoint; if any interaction code exceeds its frozen stride or an unknown user does not map to 0; if any model, rank, or blended score is non-finite; if weights are off the 1/8 simplex or do not sum to one; if sequence construction accesses a next/future row or loses/reorders an authoritative row; or if checkpoint-only final mode on the same label-free data_root fails to reproduce attempt predictions within controller tolerance. Treat transferable personalization as unsupported if fewer than 95% of chronological-holdout rows map to a prefix-seen user, if the unconstrained simplex fails to beat the reconstructed attempt-10 local primary by 0.0005 and the gate consequently freezes personalized weight at 0, or if the personalized member has effectively zero rank divergence from the proxy member. Reject the practical ensemble hypothesis unless controller primary exceeds attempt 10's 0.6600453866842653 by the campaign's frozen epsilon. If the local gate passes but controller primary misses epsilon or falls, retain attempt 10 and conclude that user-context interactions or the extra weight selection overfit the three-day holdout; do not tune codes, strides, gate, or weights from the controller result. If the gate fails, retain attempt 10 and abandon this target-free personalization family before considering any return to target encodings or sparse metadata.
card.hypothesis: Attempt 10's two globally shared context/session models apply the same tab, duration, time, session-depth, and predecessor-proxy effects to every user. Yet the training evidence shows dense histories per user and wide user-level long_view rates, so users can plausibly differ in which scenarios, duration bands, hours, session depths, and preceding-engagement states signal a long view. A third LightGBM member using only dense, target-free user-by-context categorical codes should learn those stable interaction differences without restoring the sparse video/metadata and target-rate bundle that overfit. Conservatively blending its within-user percentile ranks with the exact attempt-10 members should improve ranking when personalization transfers while preserving the parent whenever it does not.
